cooum.name: Cooum catchment
cooum.coverage: CAG performance audit 2018-19 (gap figures) + CMWSSB Sewerage System 2024 (capacity) + Cooum sewage-inlet survey
cooum.headline: The Cooum receives ~30 MLD of sewage through 31 surveyed inlets and reads among India's most polluted stretches. City-wide, 243 MLD of raw sewage reaches the rivers - but only the Cooum's inlets are actually located.
caveats: Gap figures (242.73 bypass, the per-area numbers) are CAG 2018-19 - the latest comprehensive audit; STP capacity is 2024. No newer audit publishes these.
The 242.73 MLD bypass is a CMA-wide aggregate, not split by river. 'Uncollected by sewer' is a separate measure - it goes to on-site septic tanks, not necessarily this river.

streams.summary: ~30 MLD enters the Cooum via 31 located inlets; the city-wide bypass is far larger but unlocated.

metrics.label: Located discharge into the Cooum
metrics.value: ~30.5 MLD via 31 surveyed inlets (survey)

metrics.label: Worst CPCB station
metrics.value: BOD 16 mg/L, DO 1.4 (Cooum at Poonamalle, 2024) - below Class E

metrics.label: STPs in this catchment
metrics.value: Koyambedu 214 MLD (2024 nameplate)

metrics.label: City-wide raw bypass into rivers
metrics.value: 242.73 MLD into Cooum + Adyar + Buckingham (CAG, Apr 2019); not split by river

metrics.label: Contested estimate (citizens' audit)
metrics.value: Arappor's 2018 RTI social audit puts city generation at 1,500-2,000 MLD and ~1,073 MLD into waterbodies - 2-4x the official figures; 10 of 27 audited pumping stations discharge untreated sewage directly into water bodies

metrics.label: City STP capacity (latest)
metrics.value: 934 MLD across 12 STPs at 6 sites (CMWSSB, Jan 2026) - up from 727 MLD in the 2019 CAG audit; treated volume still ~530 MLD

sources.says: 31 sewage inlets discharge into the Cooum, ~30.5 MLD combined.
An estimated 242.73 MLD of raw sewage entered storm-water drains and drained into the Adyar, Buckingham Canal and Cooum (CMA-wide).
sources.citation: CAG Report on General & Social Sector, Tamil Nadu, year ended March 2019

sources.says: Social audit of 27 pumping stations + 5 STPs (RTI + field visits): estimates Chennai generates 1,500-2,000 MLD (vs CMWSSB's 550 MLD, 2017), treats only 427 MLD, and ~1,073 MLD flows into waterbodies untreated; 10/27 pumping stations discharge untreated directly into water bodies. Alleges gross official underestimation of sewage generated.
sources.citation: Why Chennai Stinks? Citizens' report on the sewage problem, Arappor Iyakkam (civil-society / advocacy source, ~2018)

sources.says: CMWSSB operates 12 STPs at Kodungaiyur, Koyambedu, Perungudi, Nesapakkam, Sholinganallur and Tiruvottiyur with a total treatment capacity of 934 MLD.
sources.citation: Chennai Metro Water plans IoT & sentinel system for STPs, NIE, 26 Jan 2026

streams.summary: Two suburbs in this catchment have no completed sewer network; their sewage relies on on-site septic tanks.

metrics.label: Unsewered suburbs (-> septic tanks)
metrics.value: Ambattur 23.79, Avadi 4.66 MLD generated, uncollected by sewer (CAG App. 2.6, 2019)

metrics.label: Septage co-treatment (city-wide)
metrics.value: Chennai co-treats septic-tank septage at 3 STPs - Nesapakkam (~200 truck-trips/day), Perungudi (~300), Kodungaiyur (~50), ~5 MLD total (9 kL/truck) - under GoTN's Septage Management Guidelines.

metrics.label: Fate
metrics.value: On-site septic tanks. The septage is desludged by private trucks and either co-treated at an STP (the formal route) or, when dumped illegally, reaches the city's waterways - the problem the co-treatment scheme was set up to curb.

sources.says: Estimated sewage generated in delayed-UGSS (unsewered) areas, 90 LPCD: Ambattur 23.79, Avadi 4.66 MLD; city-wide total across 9 such areas = 74.69 MLD.

sources.source: FSM Toolbox - Nesapakkam STP co-treatment case study
sources.says: Chennai co-treats septage at Nesapakkam, Perungudi and Kodungaiyur STPs (52 trucks / 200 trips per day at Nesapakkam, 9 kL each). Initiated in the early 2000s to end unauthorised dumping of septage into the city's waterways by private desludging operators.
sources.citation: Nesapakkam STP Co-treatment Case Study, FSM Toolbox

adyar.name: Adyar catchment
adyar.coverage: CAG performance audit 2018-19 (gap figures) + CMWSSB Sewerage System 2024 (capacity)
adyar.headline: What actually reaches the Adyar is not separately surveyed - only the city-wide 243 MLD bypass and the six unsewered suburbs in its catchment (~30 MLD to septic tanks) are documented.
caveats: No sewage-inlet survey is published for the Adyar (only the Cooum is surveyed) - the located river-discharge here is a genuine data gap.

kosasthalaiyar.name: Kosasthalaiyar catchment
kosasthalaiyar.coverage: CAG performance audit 2018-19 (gap figures) + CMWSSB Sewerage System 2024 (capacity)
kosasthalaiyar.headline: No located river-discharge survey; one unsewered suburb (Thiruvottiyur, ~16 MLD to septic tanks) and the north-Chennai industrial belt define what's documented here.
caveats: No inlet/outfall survey is published for the Kosasthalaiyar; located river-discharge is a data gap.
Industrial effluent from the Manali/Ennore belt is not quantified here (separate industrial-water surface). Gap figures CAG 2018-19; capacity 2024.
